title: Design and implement multimodal understanding workflows

allowedScope.choice: Use a vision-capable chat model with actual images in the message when the task requires visual context.
allowedScope.configuration: Provide supported image URLs/base64 sources and a clear task; validate input limits and detail settings; constrain answers to visible evidence.
allowedScope.comparison: Text-only descriptions of a picture are not the same input as the actual picture, and visible context cannot establish hidden causes.
allowedScope.judgment: A chart analyst should cite visible axes/values and separate uncertainty from features that are actually present.

allowedScope.choice: Ask a supported multimodal model for concise or detailed descriptions, with all needed images supplied.
allowedScope.configuration: Control requested detail in the prompt and inspect whether every relevant image was included; distinguish the current multimodal route from deprecated Image Analysis examples.
allowedScope.comparison: Increasing output length does not add evidence; a fluent caption can include invented details.
allowedScope.judgment: For a comparison of two diagrams, require explicit identification of which supplied image supports each statement.

allowedScope.choice: Ground the answer in the supplied visual input and retain available extraction/source references.
allowedScope.configuration: Pass images to the visual model or use CU extraction with source coordinates/spans where supported; request uncertainty when evidence is absent.
allowedScope.comparison: Model-generated spatial descriptions are not automatically validated bounding-box detections.
allowedScope.judgment: When reading a scanned table, verify the answer against the relevant cells/source coordinates instead of trusting a plausible total.

allowedScope.choice: Generate descriptions according to the image's purpose in the page: informative, functional, decorative, or complex.
allowedScope.configuration: Use current visual models for draft descriptions; apply W3C purpose/context rules, provide extended detail for complex information, and review wording.
allowedScope.comparison: A generic caption is not an accessibility guarantee; a search-icon button needs its action described and a decorative image may need empty alt.
allowedScope.judgment: For an image-only download button, communicate the download action; for a chart, provide the meaningful data beyond a short caption.

allowedScope.choice: Configure Content Understanding to extract image characteristics or a specified schema rather than unrestricted free-form guessing.
allowedScope.configuration: Select an eligible image/document analyzer and fields; choose GA or preview API explicitly; use documentSearch for text-bearing images per the SDK reference.
allowedScope.comparison: Using an image-description analyzer for an image containing important text can lose the required document structure.
allowedScope.judgment: A catalog image description and a photo of an invoice should use analyzers suited to their different downstream representations.

allowedScope.choice: Use video extraction and configurable segmentation when analysis depends on events over time.
allowedScope.configuration: Configure whole-video or custom segments, preserve timestamps/transcripts/keyframes, and check model cost and preview limits.
allowedScope.comparison: At roughly one sampled frame per second, a single-frame incident can be missed; lower-detail frames may hide small text.
allowedScope.judgment: For a news recording, define story boundaries and keep time ranges so a summary can be checked against the clip.

evidence.statement: Content Understanding recommends the 2025-11-01 GA API for production and 2026-06-01-preview for evaluating new capabilities.

locators.heading: ## Content Understanding Features by version
locators.excerpt:
Use API version `2025-11-01` (GA) for production workloads, and use API version `2026-06-01-preview` to evaluate new capabilities announced in the Build 2026 wave.

| Capability area | `2025-11-01`(GA) | `2026-06-01-preview` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Production readiness | Recommended for production use. | Public preview for early access testing and evaluation. |
| Core multimodal extraction | Stable support for document, image, audio, and video extraction workflows. | Includes GA capabilities plus preview enhancements. |
| Agentic document understanding | Not available. | Available through [agentic mode](concepts/agentic-mode) for complex reasoning over document evidence. |
| Classification enhancements | Standard document classification and segmentation. | Adds richer classification signals and [in-page segmentation](concepts/classifier#classification-enhancements-2026-06-01-preview). |
| Document intelligence additions | Existing extraction and layout behavior. | Adds preview features such as [signature detection](document/elements#signatures) and [document metadata extraction](document/elements#document-metadata). |
| Custom analyzer training behavior | Supports labeled training examples. | Supports labeled training and improves training behavior by distilling patterns into the built analyzer for improved privacy and efficiency. See [improve analyzer training](document/analyzer-improvement). |
| Generative model flexibility | Supports GA model combinations for analyzer scenarios. | Expands and iterates model support aligned with Build 2026 updates. See [model deployments](concepts/models-deployments). |

evidence.statement: Content Understanding provides separate document, image, audio, and video search analyzers; the document-search analyzer preserves layout and structured markdown for RAG.

locators.heading: ### Prebuilt analyzers
locators.excerpt:
- **RAG analyzers** - Optimized for retrieval-augmented generation scenarios with semantic analysis and markdown extraction. These analyzers return markdown and a one-paragraph `Summary`for each content item:
    - **`prebuilt-documentSearch`** - Extracts content from documents (PDF, images, Office documents) with layout preservation, table detection, figure analysis, and structured markdown output. Optimized for RAG scenarios.
    - **`prebuilt-imageSearch`** - Analyzes standalone images and returns a one-paragraph description of the image content. Optimized for image understanding and search scenarios. For images that contain text (including hand-written text), use `prebuilt-documentSearch`.
    - **`prebuilt-audioSearch`** - Transcribes audio content with speaker diarization, timing information, and conversation summaries. Supports multilingual transcription.
    - **`prebuilt-videoSearch`** - Analyzes video content with visual frame extraction, audio transcription, and structured summaries. Provides temporal alignment of visual and audio content and can return multiple segments per video.
- **Content extraction analyzers** - Focus on OCR and layout analysis (e.g., `prebuilt-read`, `prebuilt-layout`)
- **Base analyzers** - Fundamental content processing capabilities used as parent analyzers for custom analyzers (e.g., `prebuilt-document`, `prebuilt-image`, `prebuilt-audio`, `prebuilt-video`)
- **Domain-specific analyzers** - Preconfigured analyzers for common document categories including financial documents (invoices, receipts, bank statements), identity documents (passports, driver's licenses), tax forms, mortgage documents, and contracts
- **Utility analyzers** - Specialized tools for schema generation and field extraction (e.g., `prebuilt-documentFieldSchema`, `prebuilt-documentFields`)

locators.heading: ### Configuring Microsoft Foundry resource
locators.excerpt:
### Configuring Microsoft Foundry resource

Before using the Content Understanding SDK, you need to set up a Microsoft Foundry resource and deploy the required large language models. Content Understanding currently uses OpenAI GPT models (such as gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini, and text-embedding-3-large).

evidence.statement: In the documented video configuration, enableSegment and natural-language contentCategories control whole-video versus custom segmented analysis; segmentation consumes model tokens even without fields.

locators.heading: ### Segmentation mode
locators.excerpt:
- full-length descriptive summaries
- **Custom segmentation** – `enableSegment : true` You describe the logic in natural language and the model creates segments to match. Set `contentCategories` with a string describing how you'd like the video to be segmented. Custom allows segments of varying length from seconds to minutes depending on the prompt. In this version, video only supports one `contentCategories` object.

    **Example:** Break a news broadcast up into stories.

locators.heading: ### Segmentation mode
locators.needle: Setting segmentation will use the generative model
locators.excerpt:
Setting segmentation will use the generative model, consuming tokens even if no fields are defined.

Content Understanding offers two ways to slice a video, letting you get the output you need for whole videos or short clips. You can use these options by setting the `enableSegment` property on a custom analyzer.

locators.heading: ### Segmentation mode
locators.excerpt:
- **Whole-video** – `enableSegment : false` The service treats the entire video file as a single segment and extracts metadata across its full duration.

evidence.statement: The captured video preview samples about one frame per second and resizes frames to 512 square; brief events and small or distant details can be missed.

locators.heading: ## Technical constraints and limitations
locators.excerpt:
- **Frame sampling (~ 1 FPS)**: The analyzer inspects about one frame per second. Rapid motions or single-frame events might be missed.
- **Frame resolution (512 × 512 px)**: Sampled frames are resized to 512 pixels square. Small text or distant objects can be lost.
- **Speech**: Only spoken words are transcribed. Music, sound effects, and ambient noise are ignored.

evidence.statement: Content Understanding grounding links fields to document pages, coordinates, and spans; retaining these references supports verification of downstream answers.

locators.heading: ## Grounding: Trace every result to its source
locators.excerpt:
Grounding ensures that every field, answer, or classification includes a reference to its original location in the document. This includes source information (page number and spatial coordinates) and spans (offset and length).
